title.zh: 卷五 補帝紀第五 廢帝
title.raw: 卷五 補帝紀第五 廢帝 Volume 5 Annals 5: Emperor Fei

sentences.zh: 廢帝殷，字正道，文宣帝之長子也，母曰李皇后。

translations.literal: Emperor Fei, Yin, style name Zhengdao, was the eldest son of Emperor Wenxuan; his mother was Empress Li.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Fei, whose personal name was Yin and style name Zhengdao, was the eldest son of Emperor Wenxuan. His mother was Empress Li.

sentences.zh: 天保元年，立爲皇太子，時年六歲。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao, he was installed as crown prince, aged six at the time.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tianbao era he was made crown prince, at the age of six.

sentences.zh: 性敏慧。

translations.literal: His nature was keen and clever.
translations.idiomatic: He was quick-witted by nature.

sentences.zh: 初學反語，於「跡」字下注云自反。

translations.literal: When he first studied fanqie glosses, beside the character "trace" he wrote a note saying that it glossed itself.
translations.idiomatic: When he first studied fanqie phonetic glosses, he annotated the character "trace" as self-referential.

sentences.zh: 時侍者未達其故，太子曰：「跡字足傍亦爲跡，豈非自反耶？」

translations.literal: At the time the attendants did not understand his reason; the crown prince said, "The character for trace—with the 'foot' radical beside it—is also trace; is that not a self-gloss?"
translations.idiomatic: The attendants did not understand what he meant, so the crown prince said, "The character for 'trace' has the 'foot' radical on one side and still forms 'trace'—is that not glossing itself by fanqie?"

sentences.zh: 常宴北宮，獨令河間王勿入。

translations.literal: He often held banquets in the Northern Palace and ordered the Prince of Hejian alone not to enter.
translations.idiomatic: He often gave banquets in the Northern Palace and specifically barred the Prince of Hejian from attending.

sentences.zh: 左右問其故，太子曰：「世宗遇賊處，河間王復何宜在此。」

translations.literal: Those at his side asked the reason; the crown prince said, "This is where Shizong met the assassins; the Prince of Hejian has no business being here again."
translations.idiomatic: When his attendants asked why, the crown prince said, "This is where Shizong was killed; the Prince of Hejian has no place here."

sentences.zh: 文宣每言太子得漢家性質，不似我，欲廢之，立太原王。

translations.literal: Wenxuan often said the crown prince had taken on Han Chinese temperament and was not like him; he wished to depose him and install the Prince of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan often said the crown prince had inherited Han Chinese ways and was nothing like himself; he wanted to depose him and set up the Prince of Taiyuan instead.

sentences.zh: 初詔國子博士李寶鼎傅之，寶鼎卒，復詔國子博士邢峙侍講。

translations.literal: At first an edict appointed National University erudite Li Baoding to tutor him; when Baoding died, another edict appointed National University erudite Xing Zhi to attend and lecture.
translations.idiomatic: At first an edict appointed Li Baoding, erudite of the National University, as his tutor. After Baoding died, Xing Zhi, also an erudite of the National University, was ordered to serve as his lecturer.

sentences.zh: 太子雖富於春秋，而溫裕開朗，有人君之度，貫綜經業，省覽時政，甚有美名。

translations.literal: Although the crown prince was still young in years, he was mild, generous, and open in manner, with the measure of a ruler; he mastered the classics and reviewed current affairs, and enjoyed a very fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Though still young, the crown prince was gentle, magnanimous, and open in bearing, with the bearing of a true sovereign. He had mastered the classics, kept abreast of current policy, and enjoyed an excellent reputation.

sentences.zh: 七年冬，文宣召朝臣文學者及禮學官於宮宴會，令以經義相質，親自臨聽。

translations.literal: In the winter of the seventh year, Wenxuan summoned court officials versed in letters and officers of ritual learning to a palace banquet, ordered them to examine one another on the meaning of the classics, and personally attended to listen.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the seventh year, Emperor Wenxuan summoned literary officials and ritual specialists to a palace banquet, had them debate passages from the classics, and listened in person.

sentences.zh: 太子手筆措問，在坐莫不歎美。

translations.literal: The crown prince set questions in his own hand; none of those seated failed to sigh in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince wrote out questions himself, and everyone present marveled.

sentences.zh: 九年，文宣在晉陽，太子監國，集諸儒講《孝經》。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Wenxuan was at Jinyang; the crown prince supervised the state, gathered the Confucian scholars, and lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, while Emperor Wenxuan was at Jinyang, the crown prince acted as regent, gathered the scholars, and expounded the Classic of Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 令楊愔傳旨，謂國子助教許散愁曰：「先生在世何以自資？」

translations.literal: He had Yang Yin convey the imperial message and say to National University assistant instructor Xu Sanchou, "Sir, in this life by what do you support yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: He had Yang Yin deliver his message to Xu Sanchou, assistant instructor at the National University: "Sir, how do you occupy yourself in this life?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「散愁自少以來，不登孌童之床，不入季女之室，服膺簡策，不知老之將至。

translations.literal: He replied, "Sanchou from youth onward has not mounted the couch of a catamite, has not entered the chamber of a young woman; he clings to his books and scrolls and does not know that old age is coming.
translations.idiomatic: Xu replied, "From my youth I have never shared a bed with a pretty boy or entered a maiden's room. I have devoted myself to my books and scarcely noticed that old age was upon me.

sentences.zh: 平生素懷，若斯而已。」

translations.literal: His lifelong plain intent was no more than this."
translations.idiomatic: That has been the whole of my life's ambition."

sentences.zh: 太子曰：「顏子縮屋稱貞，柳下嫗而不亂，未若此翁白首不娶者也。」

translations.literal: The crown prince said, "Yan Hui, who shrank in his hut, was called chaste; Liu Xiahui, who shared a blanket with a woman, was not corrupted—yet neither equals this old man, white-haired and never married."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince said, "Yan Hui was praised for chastity though he lived in a hovel, and Liu Xiahui kept his integrity though he shared a blanket with a woman—but neither can match this old man who has never married even to white hair."

sentences.zh: 乃賚絹百匹。

translations.literal: Thereupon he bestowed a hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He then rewarded him with a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 後文宣登金鳳台，召太子使手刃囚。

translations.literal: Later Wenxuan ascended the Golden Phoenix Terrace, summoned the crown prince, and ordered him to kill a prisoner with his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Wenxuan went up to the Golden Phoenix Terrace, called the crown prince, and ordered him to execute a prisoner with his own blade.

sentences.zh: 太子惻然有難色，再三不斷其首。

translations.literal: The crown prince looked pained and showed reluctance; again and again he could not sever the man's head.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince looked stricken and hesitated; several times he failed to strike off the man's head.

sentences.zh: 文宣怒，親以馬鞭撞太子三下，由是氣悸語吃，精神時復昏擾。

translations.literal: Wenxuan grew angry and personally struck the crown prince three blows with a horsewhip; from this he suffered palpitations and stammered in speech, and his spirit was at times again clouded and disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan flew into a rage and personally struck the crown prince three times with his riding crop. From that time on the prince suffered heart palpitations and a stammer, and his mind would sometimes grow confused.

sentences.zh: 十年十月，文宣崩。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the tenth year, Wenxuan died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the tenth year, Emperor Wenxuan died.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，太子即帝位於晉陽宣德殿，大赦，內外百官普加汎級，亡官失爵，聽復資品。

translations.literal: On the guimao day the crown prince took the imperial throne in the Xuande Hall at Jinyang, proclaimed a general amnesty, broadly raised ranks for inner and outer officials, and allowed those who had lost office or title to recover their standing.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day the crown prince ascended the throne in the Xuande Hall at Jinyang. He proclaimed a general amnesty, promoted officials throughout the government, and permitted those who had lost rank or title to recover their former status.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，尊皇太后爲太皇太后，皇后爲皇太后。

translations.literal: On the gengxu day he honored the empress dowager as grand empress dowager and the empress as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day he elevated the empress dowager to grand empress dowager and the empress to empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 詔九州軍人七十已上授以板職，武官年六十已上及癃病不堪驅使者，並皆放免。

translations.literal: An edict granted board appointments to soldiers of the nine provinces aged seventy and above; military officers sixty and above, and those crippled or ill and unfit for service, were all released and exempted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted honorary appointments to soldiers aged seventy or older throughout the realm. Military officers sixty or older, and anyone disabled or too ill for duty, were all discharged.

sentences.zh: 土木營造金銅鐵諸雜作工，一切停罷。

translations.literal: Civil construction and all miscellaneous work in gold, bronze, and iron were entirely halted.
translations.idiomatic: All civil engineering and miscellaneous work in gold, bronze, and iron was suspended.

sentences.zh: 十一月乙卯，以右丞相、咸陽王斛律金爲左丞相，以錄尚書事、常山王演爲太傅，以司徒、長廣王湛爲太尉，以司空段韶爲司徒，以平陽王淹爲司空，高陽王湜爲尚書左僕射，河間王孝琬爲司州牧，侍中燕子獻爲右僕射。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the yimao day, the right chief minister, Prince of Xianyang Hulu Jin, was made left chief minister; Prince Yan of Changshan, recorder of the affairs of the Masters of Writing, was made grand tutor; Prince Zhan of Changguang, minister over the masses, was made grand commandant; Duan Shao, minister of works, was made minister over the masses; Prince Yan of Pingyang was made minister of works; Prince Shi of Gaoyang was made left vice-director of the Masters of Writing; Prince Xiaowan of Hejian was made governor of Sizhou; and Yanzi Xian, attendant at the palace, was made right vice-director.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the yimao day, Hulu Jin, Prince of Xianyang and right chief minister, was appointed left chief minister; Prince Yan of Changshan, recorder of the Masters of Writing, became grand tutor; Prince Zhan of Changguang, minister over the masses, became grand commandant; Duan Shao, minister of works, became minister over the masses; Prince Yan of Pingyang became minister of works; Prince Shi of Gaoyang became left vice-director of the Masters of Writing; Prince Xiaowan of Hejian became governor of Sizhou; and Yanzi Xian, palace attendant, became right vice-director.

sentences.zh: 戊午，分命使者巡省四方，求政得失，省察風俗，問人疾苦。

translations.literal: On the wuwu day envoys were dispatched in separate directions to tour the four quarters, seek out the gains and losses of government, examine local customs, and inquire into the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day the court sent envoys throughout the realm to inspect government, review local customs, and learn of the people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 十二月戊戌，改封上黨王紹仁爲漁陽王，廣陽王紹義爲范陽王，長樂王紹廉爲隴西王。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the wuxu day, the Prince of Shangdang Shaoren was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Yuyang, the Prince of Guangyang Shaoyi as Prince of Fanyang, and the Prince of Changle Shaolian as Prince of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the wuxu day, Prince Shaoren of Shangdang was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Yuyang, Prince Shaoyi of Guangyang as Prince of Fanyang, and Prince Shaolian of Changle as Prince of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 是歲，周武成元年。

translations.literal: That year was the first year of Wucheng in Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: That year corresponded to the first year of the Wucheng era of Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 乾明元年庚辰，春正月癸丑朔，改元。

translations.literal: In the gengchen year, the first year of Qianming, in spring, on guichou, the first day of the first month, the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianming 1, the gengchen year, on guichou, the first day of the first month in spring, the reign era was changed.

sentences.zh: 己未，詔寬徭賦。

translations.literal: On jiwei, an edict relaxed labor services and taxes.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, an edict lightened corvee obligations and taxes.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，高陽王湜薨。

translations.literal: On guihai, Prince Shi of Gaoyang died.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, Prince Shi of Gaoyang died.

sentences.zh: 是月，車駕至自晉陽。

translations.literal: That month, the imperial carriage arrived from Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: That month the emperor returned from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 二月己亥，以太傅、常山王演爲太師、錄尚書事，以太尉、長廣王湛爲大司馬、幷省錄尚書事，以尚書左僕射、平秦王歸彥爲司空，趙郡王叡爲尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the second month, on jihai, the Grand Tutor, Prince Yan of Changshan, was made Grand Preceptor and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing; the Grand Commandant, Prince Zhan of Changguang, was made Grand Marshal and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing in Bing Province; the Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince Guiyan of Pingqin, was made Minister of Works; and Prince Rui of Zhaojun was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jihai, Prince Yan of Changshan, then grand tutor, was appointed grand preceptor and recorder of the Masters of Writing. Prince Zhan of Changguang, then grand commandant, became grand marshal and recorder of the Masters of Writing in the Bingzhou administration. Prince Guiyan of Pingqin, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, became minister of works, and Prince Rui of Zhaojun became left vice director.

sentences.zh: 詔諸元良口配沒宮內及賜人者，並放免。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that all free persons of the Yuan clan who had been assigned and confiscated into the palace or bestowed on others should all be released and exempted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict released all free members of the Yuan clan who had been confiscated into palace service or granted to others.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，帝幸芳林園，親錄囚徒，死罪以下降免各有差。

translations.literal: On jiachen, the emperor visited Fanglin Garden and personally reviewed the prisoners; those sentenced to death and below received reductions or exemptions, each by degree.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, the emperor visited Fanglin Garden and personally reviewed the prisoners. Sentences at the death penalty and below were reduced or remitted by graded degrees.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，太師、常山王演矯詔誅尚書令楊愔、尚書右僕射燕子獻、領軍大將軍可朱渾天和、侍中宋欽道、散騎常侍鄭子默。

translations.literal: On the yisi day the grand preceptor, Prince of Changshan Yan, forged an edict and executed Yang Yin, director of the Masters of Writing; Yanzi Xian, right vice-director of the Masters of Writing; Kezhuhun Tianhe, general-in-chief commanding the guards; Song Qindao, attendant at the palace; and Zheng Zimo, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day Prince Yan of Changshan, grand preceptor, forged an edict and had executed Yang Yin, director of the Masters of Writing; Yanzi Xian, right vice-director; Kezhuhun Tianhe, commanding general of the palace guards; Song Qindao, palace attendant; and Zheng Zimo, attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 戊申，以常山王演爲大丞相、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事，以大司馬、長廣王湛爲太傅、京畿大都督，以司徒段韶爲大將軍，以前司空、平陽王淹爲太尉，以司空、平秦王歸彥爲司徒，彭城王浟爲尚書令。

translations.literal: On the wushen day, Prince Yan of Changshan was made grand chief minister, commander-in-chief of all armies at home and abroad, and recorder of the affairs of the Masters of Writing; Prince Zhan of Changguang, grand marshal, was made grand tutor and metropolitan commander of the capital region; Duan Shao, minister over the masses, was made great general; the former minister of works, Prince Yan of Pingyang, was made grand commandant; Prince Guiyan of Pingqin, minister of works, was made minister over the masses; and Prince You of Pengcheng was made director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On the wushen day, Prince Yan of Changshan was appointed grand chief minister, commander of all armies, and recorder of the Masters of Writing. Prince Zhan of Changguang, grand marshal, became grand tutor and metropolitan commander of the capital region. Duan Shao, minister over the masses, became great general; Prince Yan of Pingyang, formerly minister of works, became grand commandant; Prince Guiyan of Pingqin, minister of works, became minister over the masses; and Prince You of Pengcheng became director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 又以高麗王世子湯爲使持節、領東夷校尉、遼東郡公、高麗王。

translations.literal: The heir of the king of Goguryeo, Tang, was also appointed bearer of the staff of authority, colonel of the Eastern Yi, Duke of Liaodong commandery, and King of Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Tang, crown prince of Goguryeo, was also appointed bearer of the imperial staff, colonel of the Eastern Yi, Duke of Liaodong commandery, and King of Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 是月，王琳爲陳所敗，蕭莊自拔至和州。

translations.literal: That month Wang Lin was defeated by Chen; Xiao Zhuang escaped on his own to Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: That month Wang Lin was defeated by Chen forces, and Xiao Zhuang fled on his own to Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 三月甲寅，詔軍國事皆申晉陽，稟大丞相常山王規算。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the jiayin day, an edict ordered that all military and state affairs be reported to Jinyang and decided according to the plans of the grand chief minister, Prince of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the jiayin day, an edict declared that all military and civil affairs were to be referred to Jinyang for decision by the grand chief minister, Prince Yan of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 壬申，封文襄第二子孝珩爲廣甯王，第三子長恭爲蘭陵王。

translations.literal: On renshen, Wenxiang's second son Xiaoheng was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangning, and his third son Changgong as Prince of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Xiaoheng, Wenxiang's second son, was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangning, and Changgong, his third son, as Prince of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 夏四月癸亥，詔河南、定、冀、趙、瀛、滄、南膠、光、青九州，往因螽水，頗傷時稼，遣使分途贍恤。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on the guihai day, an edict addressed the nine provinces Henan, Ding, Ji, Zhao, Ying, Cang, Nanjiao, Guang, and Qing: in the past locusts and floods had greatly harmed the season's crops, and envoys were sent by separate routes to provide relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on the guihai day, an edict to the nine provinces of Henan, Ding, Ji, Zhao, Ying, Cang, Nanjiao, Guang, and Qing noted that locusts and floods had lately damaged the harvest, and dispatched envoys along separate routes to provide relief.

sentences.zh: 是月，周明帝崩。

translations.literal: That month Emperor Ming of Zhou died.
translations.idiomatic: That month Emperor Ming of Northern Zhou died.

sentences.zh: 五月壬子，以開府儀同三司劉洪徽爲尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the renzi day, Liu Honghui, opener of the government with ritual parity of the three excellencies, was made right vice-director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the renzi day, Liu Honghui, holder of the honorific opener of the government with ritual parity of the three excellencies, was appointed right vice-director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 秋八月壬午，太皇太后令廢帝爲濟南王，令食一郡，以大丞相、常山王演入纂大統。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn, on the renwu day, the grand empress dowager ordered Emperor Fei demoted to Prince of Jinan, granted the revenue of one commandery, and the grand chief minister, Prince of Changshan Yan, to enter and succeed to the great succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn, on the renwu day, the grand empress dowager deposed Emperor Fei as Prince of Jinan with the income of a single commandery, and installed the grand chief minister, Prince Yan of Changshan, as successor to the throne.

sentences.zh: 是日，王居別宮。

translations.literal: That day the prince resided in a separate palace.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the deposed emperor moved to a separate palace.

sentences.zh: 皇建二年九月，殂於晉陽，年十七。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Huangjian he died at Jinyang, aged seventeen.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second year of the Huangjian era he died at Jinyang, at the age of seventeen.

sentences.zh: 帝聰慧夙成，寬厚仁智，天保間雅有令名。

translations.literal: The emperor was intelligent and wise from an early age, generous, kind, benevolent, and discerning; during Tianbao he had a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed intelligence early, was generous and humane, and during the Tianbao era enjoyed an excellent reputation.

sentences.zh: 及承大位，楊愔、燕子獻、宋欽道等同輔。

translations.literal: When he inherited the great throne, Yang Yin, Yanzi Xian, Song Qindao, and others assisted him together.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to the throne, Yang Yin, Yanzi Xian, Song Qindao, and others served jointly as his advisers.

sentences.zh: 以常山王地親望重，內外畏服，加以文宣初崩之日，太后本欲立之，故愔等並懷猜忌。

translations.literal: Because the Prince of Changshan was close in kinship and weighty in reputation, and those within and without feared and submitted to him, and because on the day Emperor Wenxuan first died the empress dowager had originally wanted to enthrone him, Yin and the others all harbored suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yan of Changshan was a close kinsman with formidable prestige, feared and obeyed at court and beyond. Since the empress dowager had originally wanted to enthrone him when Emperor Wenxuan died, Yang Yin and the others all suspected him.

sentences.zh: 常山王憂悵，乃白太后誅其黨，時平秦王歸彥亦預謀焉。

translations.literal: The Prince of Changshan became anxious and distressed, and so reported to the empress dowager that their party should be executed; at the time Prince Guiyan of Pingqin also took part in the plot.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yan of Changshan grew anxious and asked the empress dowager to execute that faction; Prince Guiyan of Pingqin was also involved in the plot.

sentences.zh: 皇建二年秋，天文告變，歸彥慮有後害，仍白孝昭，以王當咎。

translations.literal: In autumn of the second year of Huangjian, celestial signs announced change; Guiyan feared there would be later danger, and again told Xiaozhao that the prince was the one on whom blame would fall.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of Huangjian 2, ominous celestial signs appeared. Guiyan feared future trouble and again told Emperor Xiaozhao that the prince was the one portended by the omen.

sentences.zh: 乃遣歸彥馳驛至晉陽宮殺之。

translations.literal: He therefore sent Guiyan by relay horse to Jinyang Palace to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore sent Guiyan by relay post to Jinyang Palace to kill him.

sentences.zh: 王薨後，孝昭不豫，見文宣爲祟。

translations.literal: After the prince died, Xiaozhao fell ill and saw Wenxuan acting as a baleful spirit.
translations.idiomatic: After the prince died, Emperor Xiaozhao fell ill and saw Emperor Wenxuan haunting him as an angry spirit.

sentences.zh: 孝昭深惡之，厭勝術備設而無益也。

translations.literal: Xiaozhao deeply hated it, and suppressive apotropaic rites were set up in every form, but they were of no benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhao was terrified and deployed every rite for suppressing baleful influence, but none helped.

sentences.zh: 薨三旬而孝昭崩。

translations.literal: Thirty days after the prince died, Xiaozhao died.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty days after the prince died, Emperor Xiaozhao died as well.

sentences.zh: 大寧二年，葬於武寧之西北，諡閔悼王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daning he was buried northwest of Wuning and was posthumously titled Prince Mindao.
translations.idiomatic: In Daning 2 he was buried northwest of Wuning and given the posthumous title Prince Mindao.

sentences.zh: 初，文宣命邢卲制帝名殷，字正道，帝從而尤之曰：「殷家弟及，『正』字一止，吾身後兒不得也。」

translations.literal: Initially, Emperor Wenxuan ordered Xing Shao to devise the emperor's personal name Yin and style Zhengdao; the emperor then faulted him, saying, "In the house of Yin, younger brothers succeeded; the character zheng contains one stop, so after I am gone my son will not get it."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Wenxuan had ordered Xing Shao to devise Yin as the emperor's personal name and Zhengdao as his style. Wenxuan later faulted him for it: "In the house of Yin, brothers succeeded one another, and the character 正 contains a single 'stop.' After I am gone, my son will not have it."

sentences.zh: 卲懼，請改焉。

translations.literal: Shao was afraid and asked to change it.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was frightened and asked to change the names.

sentences.zh: 文宣不許曰：「天也。」

translations.literal: Wenxuan did not permit it and said, "It is Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan refused, saying, "It is Heaven."

sentences.zh: 因謂孝昭帝曰：「奪但奪，慎勿殺也。」

translations.literal: He then told Emperor Xiaozhao, "If you seize it, just seize it; be careful not to kill him."
translations.idiomatic: He then told Emperor Xiaozhao, "If you take it, take it, but be careful not to kill him."

sentences.zh: 論曰：濟南繼業，大革其弊，風教粲然，搢紳稱幸。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Jinan inherited the enterprise, greatly reformed its abuses, and teaching and customs shone brightly; the gentry considered themselves fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: Jinan inherited the enterprise and greatly reformed its abuses. Teaching and custom shone brightly, and the gentry counted themselves fortunate.

sentences.zh: 股肱輔弼，雖懷厥誠，旣不能贊弘道德，和睦親懿，又不能遠慮防身，深謀衛主，應斷不斷，自取其咎。

translations.literal: His chief ministers and assistants, although they held sincere intentions, could neither assist him in magnifying the Way and virtue and harmonizing his close kin, nor plan farsightedly to protect themselves and deeply scheme to safeguard their lord; when they should have acted decisively they did not, and brought blame upon themselves.
translations.idiomatic: His chief ministers may have been sincere, but they could not help him enlarge the Way and virtue or keep harmony among his kin. Nor could they plan far enough to protect themselves or safeguard their lord. When decision was needed they failed to decide, and brought disaster on themselves.

sentences.zh: 臣旣誅夷，君壽廢辱，皆任非其器之所致爾。

translations.literal: The ministers were already executed and wiped out, while the ruler, though alive, was deposed and humiliated; all this came from entrusting office to men who were not equal to the task.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers were exterminated, and the ruler, though still alive, was deposed and humiliated. All of it came from entrusting affairs to men unequal to the task.
